chapter: Earl Hines, Chicago and later gigs
title: Martha Raye singing at the Grand Terrace; Joe E. Lewis
summary: A young Martha Raye sang with the band after her Loop job; Sally Rand and Joe E. Lewis were around in 1933.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: You were saying that there were a whole lot more things about Earl Hines than that you wanted to talk about.

Yeah, there are a lot of things about Earl, because I find that when I work -- when I did work with Earl in Chicago, there was a young singer that -- Caucasian girl that used to come out and sing with us at night after she got through her work down in the Loop. She was singing -- I'm not sure if it was Ted Fiorito's band, but I know it was one of those bands of that sort that she sang with down the Loop.
And "Truckin" had just become popular. And she used to come out there, and she could really dance a while on "Truckin". She sang funny. She did a lot of comedy things. And that was Martha Raye.

And Martha Raye came and her mother used to come with her. Her mother's name was Peggy. And she used to come out there with her a lot of times. And Martha and I were talking about this in Honolulu about a couple of months
ago. She came over to do a show, a benefit show I think. It wasn't -- it was a variety show over there. And she came to do it for the kids over there in a variety club.

And we were talking about that then. She used to come out there and sing all the time, man, you know with us at (Unintelligible) night after our last show, you know. And we stayed open to 4:00, and she got through down the Loop about 12:00 or 12:30. And they'd come out there and, boy, after the last show, after about 1:30 the last show, well, we'd just jam it out the rest of the night. She'd sing with us, man. She would really sing too.
I never forgot her. This is before she ever got big, you know. This is the same time that Sally Rand was getting big at the World's Fair in Chicago. At the same -- around the same period of time.

That's right. And Joe E. Lewis was a comedian out in Cicero at that time. He used to come by a lot of times by the Grand Terrace. They all used to come by there a lot. Joe Louis, the fighter, he was coming up there and he used to come by a lot. And the reason Joe E. Lewis said he named himself with the E. was because he didn't want to get mixed up with Joe Louis, the fighter. The names were spelled different, Lewis, but they were pronounced the same, see.
